cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: I wanted to have a chat with you because our friend Josh told me that you've joined a

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: guitar group and it sounds interesting. I'd really like to learn myself.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: Why don't you come along? I'm sure there's room for another person.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: He's called a 'coordinator' – his name's Gary Mathieson.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: Let me note that down. Gary. . . . How do you spell his surname?

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: He's retired, actually, but he's a really nice guy and he used to play in a lot of bands.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: And could you play anything before you started?

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: That's what I thought, too.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: When I first spoke to Gary on the phone, he said it was a class for beginners, but I was

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: still worried that everyone would be better than me, but we were all equally hopeless!

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: Well, when I joined the group, they were meeting in Gary's home, but as the group got

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: bigger, he decided to book a room at the college in town. I prefer going there.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: I know that place.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: I used to go to tap dancing classes there when I was at secondary school.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: I haven't been since, though and I can't remember what road it's in… is it Lock Street?

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: It's just beyond there at the bottom of New Street near the city roundabout.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: The guitar club is on the first floor in Room T347.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: Right. And when do you meet? Is it at the weekend?

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: We meet on Thursdays. It used to be 10.30 and that suited me well, but now we meet at 11.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: The class that's in there before us asked if they could have the room for another 30

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: minutes.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: Oh, I see. Well, I'd love to come, but I don't have a guitar.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: Well, you can always buy a second-hand one.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: There's a website called 'The perfect instrument' that sells all kinds of guitars,

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: violins and so on. I'm sure you'll find something there.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: Well, he always starts by getting us to tune our guitars. That takes about five minutes.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: Some people have an app they use, but others do it by ear. Gary goes round and helps them.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: And while he's doing that, he tells us what he's going to do during the lesson.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: First, we usually spend about ten minutes doing some strumming.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: So is that using . . . what are they called . . . plectrums?

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: Gary reminds us where to put our fingers for each chord and then we play them together.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: Sometimes we all just start laughing because we're so bad at keeping time, so Gary starts

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: clapping to help us.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: Yes – we do at least one song with words and chords. I mean that's harder than you think.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: That part of the lesson takes about 15 minutes.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: He often brings a recording of the song and plays it to us first.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: Then he hands out the song and if there's a new chord in it, we practise that before we

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: play it together – but really slowly.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: That's the last ten minutes of the lesson, when we pick out the individual notes from a

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: tune he's made up. It's always quite simple.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: It is, but people like it because they can really concentrate and if we're all playing

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: well, it sounds quite impressive.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: The only trouble is that he sometimes gets us to play one at a time – you know, alone.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: It is, but I've got used to it now.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: At the end he spends about five minutes telling us what to practise for the following

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: week.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: Well, thanks Coleman. I'll go and have a look at that website, I think.
